body.statement: For every compatible \(p\), the identified set \(\{\theta_{ab}(q):q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\}\) is exactly \([L_T(p),U_T(p)]\), where \(L_T(p)=\kappa-D_T(p)=\max_{f\in\mathfrak F^-_T}f(p)\) and \(U_T(p)=-L_T(\bar p)=\min_{f\in\mathfrak F^+_T}f(p)\). Each endpoint list contains the eight Balke--Pearl affine pieces and exactly two additional evaluation pieces \(C^-_{c,0},C^-_{c,1}\), or \(C^+_{c,0},C^+_{c,1}\), for every \(c\in T\setminus\{a,b\}\); no affine inequality involving several nuisance categories lowers or raises an endpoint beyond this envelope. The finite laws \(q^-_T(p)\) and \(q^+_T(p)\) attain the two endpoints, and their mixtures attain every interior value. As a one-line corollary, if \(T'=T\cup\{c\}\) is compatible, then \(L_{T'}(p)=\max\{L_T(p),C^-_{c,0}(p),C^-_{c,1}(p)\}\) and \(U_{T'}(p)=\min\{U_T(p),C^+_{c,0}(p),C^+_{c,1}(p)\}\), with strict width reduction exactly when \(\max_yC^-_{c,y}(p)>L_T(p)\) or \(\min_yC^+_{c,y}(p)<U_T(p)\).
body.justification: This theorem resolves the arbitrary-cardinality mixed-validity projection and isolates the linear-size closed form.
body.gap: Gabriel et al. stop at small treatment supports, while Song et al. require exclusion at every category and leave the pairwise effect as a general optimization.
body.consumer: The theorem lets LEAP investigators decide whether separately defensible intermediate adherence interventions can change the low-versus-high interval without rerunning symbolic polyhedral elimination.
